newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates steady in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates steady in latest week.

text.p: Rates on fixed-rate mortgages edged higher this week while adjustable-rate loans fell, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.
The agency said 30-year mortgage rates averaged 7.88 percent this week, up from 7.86 percent last week, and 15-year loans rose to 7.39 percent from 7.38 percent.
Adjustable-rate mortgages fell to an average 5.62 percent from 5.68 percent.
A year ago, 30-year fixed-rate loans averaged 7.38 percent, 15-year loans stood at 6.92 percent and one-year adjustable loans were 5.72 percent.

Rates higher than a year ago and a slowing economy may be taking a toll on the housing market. The Commerce Department said in a separate report Thursday that housing starts fell 6.0 percent last month after a 4.0 percent gain in August.
Lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans, and 1.4 percent on adjustable loans, all unchanged from the previous week, the agency said.
